title: WordPress WP2Shell Chained Takeover (CVE-2026-60137 + CVE-2026-63030)
description: A chained WordPress takeover ("WP2Shell") combining CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030, reported by Talos. Attackers chain the two vulnerabilities to exploit externally facing WordPress sites. Public evidence is sparse: the only concrete indicators are the "WP2Shell" name and the two CVE identifiers, so all post-exploitation behavior is modeled as behavioral rather than asserted.

simulation_steps.title: Reconnaissance and vulnerability probing
simulation_steps.description: Attackers probe externally facing WordPress sites for the chained vulnerabilities.

simulation_steps.title: Chained exploitation (CVE-2026-60137 + CVE-2026-63030)
simulation_steps.description: The two vulnerabilities are chained to exploit the public-facing application.

simulation_steps.title: Successful takeover (behavioral)
simulation_steps.description: Behavioral indicators of takeover follow: anomalous successful admin sessions, unexpected content changes and outbound connections. Specific post-exploitation techniques are not asserted due to sparse public evidence.

simulation_steps.title: Detect exploitation attempts
simulation_steps.description: Blue team detects anomalous request bursts and exploitation signatures against the WordPress attack surface.

simulation_steps.title: Detect post-takeover anomalies (behavioral)
simulation_steps.description: Blue team correlates successful admin sessions, content changes and outbound connections as behavioral takeover indicators.

simulation_steps.title: Contain and remediate
simulation_steps.description: SOC patches the vulnerabilities, isolates affected sites, resets credentials and restores from known-good backups.
